title: Senior Management Accountability
summary: An eight-module programme helping executives and senior managers understand their personal accountability and evidence reasonable steps under senior manager regimes.
intro: This training programme equips executives and senior managers to understand and discharge their personal obligations under senior manager accountability and certification regimes, and to evidence the reasonable steps they take.

sections.Aim and Purpose: To give executives and senior managers a clear, practical understanding of individual accountability: what they are responsible for, what reasonable steps look like, and how authorities judge failure. Participants leave able to define their responsibilities, oversee what they delegate and evidence their decisions in a way that stands up to supervisory and enforcement scrutiny.
sections.What It Covers: The purpose of senior manager accountability regimes, statements of responsibilities, the duty of responsibility and reasonable steps, delegation, oversight and handovers, conduct rules and fitness and propriety, evidencing reasonable steps, lessons from enforcement cases, and personal accountability for AI and technology decisions.
Intended Audience: Executive directors, senior managers and heads of business lines holding senior manager functions
Heads of compliance, risk, internal audit and other control functions with personal accountability
Company secretaries, HR and compliance staff who administer the accountability regime
Learning Objectives: Explain the purpose and building blocks of senior manager accountability and certification regimes
Define personal responsibilities clearly in statements of responsibilities
Apply the duty of responsibility and the reasonable steps test to real scenarios
Design delegation, oversight and handover arrangements that preserve accountability
Evidence reasonable steps through proportionate, contemporaneous records
Assess personal accountability for AI and technology and see the firm the way a supervisor does
sections.Structure and Format: Eight modules of about three hours each, delivered in person, virtually or in a hybrid format, either as a multi-day programme or as a series of half-day sessions. Modules combine short briefings with scenario exercises, generic enforcement cases and group discussion, and can be selected or tailored to the firm's accountability framework.
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some management experience in a regulated firm is helpful. No legal background is required.
Core Reading: FSB, Strengthening Governance Frameworks to Mitigate Misconduct Risk: A Toolkit for Firms and Supervisors (2018)
Group of Thirty, Banking Conduct and Culture: A Call for Sustained and Comprehensive Reform (2015)
Basel Committee, Corporate Governance Principles for Banks (2015)

modules.title: Why Senior Manager Accountability Regimes Exist
modules.summary: The origins and purpose of senior manager accountability and certification regimes, the gaps they were designed to close, and how they change the personal position of executives.
objectives: Explain the policy rationale for individual accountability in financial services
Describe the common building blocks of senior manager and certification regimes
Identify how these regimes change the personal exposure of senior managers
syllabus: Lessons from past failures where no one was held accountable
Senior manager functions, certified staff and conduct rules
International approaches and the FSB toolkit on misconduct risk
What supervisors now expect of individual senior managers

modules.title: Statements of Responsibility and Responsibilities Maps
modules.summary: How responsibilities are allocated, documented and kept current, and how to write a statement of responsibilities that is clear, complete and defensible.
objectives: Draft a clear and accurate statement of responsibilities
Assess the firm's responsibilities map for gaps and overlaps
Keep allocations current through change and restructuring
syllabus: Prescribed responsibilities and business area responsibilities
Drafting principles: precision, completeness and avoiding shared ownership
Responsibilities maps, governance arrangements and reporting lines
Common drafting weaknesses identified by supervisors

modules.title: The Duty of Responsibility and Reasonable Steps
modules.summary: What the duty of responsibility means in practice, how reasonable steps are judged, and the factors an authority weighs when deciding whether a senior manager fell short.
objectives: Explain the duty of responsibility and the reasonable steps test
Identify the factors used to judge whether steps were reasonable
Apply the test to realistic scenarios involving failures in the senior manager's area
syllabus: The duty of responsibility: scope, burden and consequences
What counts as reasonable: knowledge, resources, urgency and hindsight
Acting on red flags, escalation and seeking expert advice
Scenario exercise: did the senior manager take reasonable steps

modules.title: Delegation, Oversight and Handovers
modules.summary: How senior managers delegate without abdicating responsibility, oversee what they have delegated, and manage handovers so that accountability does not fall between the gaps.
objectives: Delegate tasks while retaining effective oversight and accountability
Design management information and challenge that evidence oversight
Plan and document an effective handover on joining or leaving a role
syllabus: Delegation versus abdication: what remains with the senior manager
Oversight tools: management information, assurance and challenge
Reliance on committees, control functions and group entities
Handover certificates, reading in and the first hundred days

modules.title: Conduct Rules, Fitness and Propriety
modules.summary: The conduct standards that apply to senior managers and wider staff, and the ongoing assessment of fitness and propriety, including how the firm certifies and monitors individuals.
objectives: Explain the individual and senior manager conduct rules
Apply fitness and propriety criteria at appointment and on an ongoing basis
Identify breaches, reporting obligations and regulatory references
syllabus: Individual conduct rules and the additional senior manager rules
Honesty, integrity, competence and financial soundness
Annual certification, regulatory references and breach reporting
Non-financial misconduct and its treatment under the regime

modules.title: Evidencing Reasonable Steps
modules.summary: How senior managers create a contemporaneous record that shows they understood their area, acted on risks and escalated issues, without generating defensive paperwork.
objectives: Identify the records that best evidence reasonable steps
Design a personal accountability file proportionate to the role
Use minutes, challenge and escalation records to evidence decisions
syllabus: What good evidence looks like: contemporaneous, specific and decision-focused
Board and committee minutes as evidence of challenge
Personal accountability files, attestations and their limits
Avoiding box-ticking and defensive documentation

modules.title: Enforcement Cases and Lessons Learned
modules.summary: What enforcement and supervisory interventions against senior managers reveal about where individuals go wrong, how investigations unfold and how to respond if under scrutiny.
objectives: Analyse generic enforcement cases against senior managers
Explain the stages of an investigation into an individual
Identify the behaviours that most often lead to individual action
syllabus: Typical failings: ignored warnings, inadequate oversight and poor escalation
Investigation process: interviews, representations and outcomes
Sanctions: prohibition, fines, suspension and remuneration consequences
Personal protection: legal advice, insurance and indemnities

modules.title: Personal Accountability for AI and Technology Decisions
modules.summary: Applies the regime to AI, technology change and third-party dependency, and closes with a personal action plan for each participant's accountabilities.
objectives: Identify who is accountable for AI, technology and outsourcing decisions
Apply the reasonable steps test to technology failures and AI-driven harm
Produce a personal accountability action plan
syllabus: Allocating responsibility for AI models, data and automated decisions
Major technology change, outages and third-party failures
Questions a senior manager should ask before approving AI use
Workshop: my accountabilities, evidence and twelve-month action plan

related.title: Board Effectiveness: Dynamics and Decision-Making
related.summary: A ten-module programme helping boards strengthen their dynamics, information and decision-making, and evidence effective oversight to supervisors.

related.title: Culture, Conduct and Accountability for Boards
related.summary: An eight-module programme giving boards the tools to shape and oversee culture, align incentives, hold individuals to account and evidence oversight to regulators.

related.title: Effective Governance for Boards and Directors
related.summary: A twelve-module programme covering the standards expected of individual directors and the practices that make a board effective, for regulated firms, fund boards and management companies.

related.title: Finance and Prudential Essentials for Directors of Regulated Firms
related.summary: An eight-module programme giving non-financial directors the confidence to read a regulated firm's accounts, capital and liquidity position, and to challenge the CFO.

related.title: Geopolitical and Emerging Risks for Boards
related.summary: An eight-module programme helping boards identify, debate and prepare for geopolitical and emerging risks, ending with a facilitated board scenario exercise.

related.title: Group Governance and Cross-Border Operations
related.summary: A nine-module programme helping boards and senior managers of cross-border groups balance group direction with local accountability, oversee intragroup arrangements and deal with multiple supervisors.
